- Found in a treasure chest in a room locked by an Imp Statue located at the lower level near the Prayer Room Site of Grace.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown: Throws out 3 wide rings of light in a 90-degree arc that has Holy Attack Power equal to 155% of Incantation Scaling and pierces through enemies, stopping upon hitting an object. They still cause damage when stopped and return to the caster 2 seconds after stopping, having the same amount of Attack Power on the returning hit.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 28 points of Stamina to cast.
- Deals 3 Stance damage per hit, for up to 9 Stance damage if all hits land.
- Attack Power is boosted by 10% per Golden Order Seal held in an active hand (2 max) and by 15% per Dryleaf Seal held in an active hand (2 max).
 - Since it's possible to acquire both of these Seals in one Playthrough, it's one of a few spells able to stack Seal boosts (for a total boost of 27% in this case).
- Wearing the Radiant Gold Mask increases Attack Power by 10%.
- Effectively has Attack Power equal to 310% of Incantation Scaling per ring since it will very often hit the main target on the way back.
 - Can potentially hit with Attack Power equal to 465% of Incantation Scaling if the target is also standing at the incantation's maximum range or at a hit object (or hit ground).
 - Note that the rings share hit registration, meaning an enemy can only be hit up to 3 times: once when the ring is thrown out, a second time when it's stopped, and a third possible hit when the rings return.
- Several rings can be out at the same time, making the spell very spammable.
 - If casting the spell sequentially, the first set of rings will start to return as the second set is being thrown out.
- Pairs decently well with the Erdtree Greatshield's skill Golden Retaliation and the Ash of War: Carian Retaliation since the timing of the returning ring is very predictable and will trigger the spell-parry-into-projectile part of those skills.
- The caster takes a short step forwards each time the spell is cast. While many steep falls prevent a character from stepping over them from movement caused by Skills, Spells, and Weapons, it's still good to be a bit careful.
- Though it goes through all enemies, it will not ignore the damage reduction from an enemy that is keeping its guard up if they are guarding in the direction it's flying from.
 - Note that it will still fly through said guarding enemy and will hit their unprotected back when returning unless said enemy turns around in between the two hits.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.07 increased casting speed.
- Patch 1.04 increased damage.
 - Attack Power was increased from 134% of Incantation Scaling to 155% of Incantation Scaling.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Trolls were an intelligent race of a lesser giants that inhabited the Lands Between, performing divine smithing rites with braided stone hammers.
Much smaller than their gargantuan progenitors, they betrayed the ancient Fire Giants during the War Against the Giants, tipping the scales in favor of Queen Marika's forces. Those who fought for the Erdtree received swords gilded in gold, while those who fell were interred in the Giant-Conquering Hero's Grave.

When the golden armies of Leyndell threatened the sovereignty of Liurnia of the Lakes, the Carians, heirs of ancient astrologers, invoked an old oath and called the Trolls to arms. As fully-fledged Carian Knights, the enchanted Troll Knights served beside the young Queen Rennala, twice repelling the forces of Radagon during the Liurnian Wars.

Many Trolls fought in the Shattering, serving various Demigods. Some joined with ousted Golden Lineage loyalists in the Second Defense of Leyndell, others aided the Redmanes in staving off Malenia's scarlet rot. Dozens perished in the bloody Assault on Volcano Manor, their corpses strung up and hanged by their feet. By the end of the conflict, most Trolls lost their wits, succumbed to madness, or became beasts of burden, pulling Great Coffin carriages across the land.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown:
Trolls are broad, muscular humanoids of towering stature. Two great whiskers hang from their faces, which are enwreathed in a grand mane of smaller, root-like growths. A stone slab is embedded within the open chest cavity of each troll, held in place by thick roots. Sometimes, stakes are lodged into these cavities, allowing the trolls to drag carriages along behind them. They can be found throughout the Lands Between, often fighting on behalf of various armies and factions. The earth shakes when they stomp, and their roars produce gales of wind. Trolls who wield golden swords typically draw them upon losing half of their HP.

Most of their attacks are slow and heavily telegraphed, making them easy to punish even with larger weapons. Trolls frequently expose themselves due to their sluggish movement and lengthy attack recoveries. Their main counter to close-range pressure is a stomp, which can be chained several times to push players out of their blind spots. They all share a basic unarmed moveset of forward fist slams, broad arm sweeps, quick stomps, and a leaping two-handed spike. Sword-bearing Trolls add slow, heavily delayed slashes and up to three consecutive dashing swings. They also possess a long-range roar that sends out a fast shockwave, and many of their melee attacks create splash damage.

Most Trolls are susceptible to all common status ailments. Applying both Poison and Scarlet Rot simultaneously can drain up to half their HP. Blood Loss is also effective. Their greatest vulnerability is to Sleep—a single St. Trina's Arrow will sedate them, allowing for either a high-damage Critical Hit, or continuous attacks during their extended recovery animation, possibly inflicting additional ailments.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
A bolt of red lightning strikes down on the caster's weapon, granting them a Weapon Buff that gives Lightning Attack Power equal to 75% of Faith-based Incantation Scaling and a Body Buff that increases maximum Equip Load by 15% but lowers Lightning Damage Negation.

Both buffs last for 70 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs 20 points of Stamina to cast.
- The Weapon Buff and the Body Buff are separate effects, meaning that the Body Buff remains active if the Weapon Buff is deactivated and vice versa.
 - The effective change to current Equip Load depends on how high the Equip Load was beforehand. To compare, someone at 30% Equip Load would have it lowered to 26.1%, someone at 70% Equip Load would have it lowered to 60.9%, and someone at 100% Equip Load would have it lowered to 87%.
- This spell can only be cast if the wielded right-hand weapon can be buffed by spells, though the Body Buff can still be taken advantage of by keeping a light, buffable weapon such as a Dagger or Caestus in an extra weapon slot.
- Lightning damage is fairly rare outside of Leyndell, Royal Capital and Crumbling Farum Azula, making the downside of the Body Buff often irrelevant unless fighting other players.
- The Weapon Buff portion is equally as strong as Electrify Armament.
- Outmatched by Lightning Grease and Skill: Lightning Slash below 114 Incantation Scaling and by Dragonbolt Grease Shadow of the Erdtree below 160 Incantation Scaling.
 - Though they cast much quicker and last for a shorter duration, Drawstring Lightning Grease is stronger below 147 Incantation Scaling while Drawstring Dragonbolt Grease Shadow of the Erdtree is stronger below 180 Incantation Scaling.
 - Lightning Slash has the advantage of also being usable for weapons with the otherwise unbuffable (not counting other skills) Lightning and Sacred Affinity weapons.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Volcano Manor** (火山館, *Kazan-kan*) is a subregion in Elden Ring. It is a legacy dungeon located on Mt. Gelmir.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
During the Shattering, the Volcano Manor was the home of Praetor Rykard and his Recusant, fierce warriors who waged war against the Erdtree. Following Rykard's transformation into the Lord of Blasphemy, the remaining Recusants deserted him and left the Volcano Manor. Afterwards, Rykard's consort, Lady Tanith, continued to maintain the Manor as the base of operations for a new generation of Recusants. After their return to the Lands Between, Tarnished considered strong and merciless towards their kin, were extended invitations to join the Volcano Manor and are given contracts to hunt other Tarnished in service of the Roundtable. Tarnished who prove themselves are offered an audience with what has become of Praetor Rykard, the Lord of Blasphemy, which will inevitably end with the serpentine demigod devouring them for their strength.

Even after the Shattering, the Volcano Manor is still besieged by the forces of the Royal Capital. Camps of Leyndell soliders dot the perilous assent of Mt. Gelmir.

sections.heading: Walkthrough
sections.markdown:
The Volcano Manor is one of the game's most complex locations. It can be reached in multiple ways and you can progress through from different directions.

The fastest, but most gimmicky way to reach it is by letting the Abductor Virgin at the bottom of the Raya Lucaria Academy grapple you to death. You will still drop your runes, but be respawned right within the Volcano Manor area. From here there are two paths that are each a point of no return. One leading to the rest of the manor, the other brings you to the Abductor Virgin duo bossfight and back to the Altus Plateau. For the Abductor Virgin boss, search for the cave with multiple drop-down platforms. To progress deeper into the manor, jump down the lava waterfall. If you die here before reaching a grace, you will be respawned where the Abductor Virgin dropped you within Volcano Manor. From here you can explore the area, defeat the Godskin Noble and either make it back to the manor entrance with Lady Tanith and the other npcs, or skip their quests and head straight to the gateway portal leading to Praetor Rykard.

The regular paths to enter the manor are either on foot/horseback across Mt. Gelmir, or to be teleported right to the Volcano Manor entrance grace by Rya once reaching the Altus Plateau. You won't be able to reach the bosses or explore the rest of the area from here unless you accept Lady Tanith's offer to get the Drawing-Room Key. If you join the manor, a list of NPCs become available there: Bernahl, Patches, Rya, Diallos Hoslow. To get all the content out of the manor, you have to wait with fighting Rykard until reaching the Mountaintops of the Giants, so that you can do all of the following NPC invasions for the manor: Old Knight Istvan, Rileigh the Idle, Great Horned Tragoth, Vargram the Raging Wolf + Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm, Juno Hoslow, Knight of Blood. After defeating Juno Hoslow, Tanith offers to send you to Rykard, where you can then start the boss fight. Remember to complete Rya's quest before defeating Juno Hoslow, Knight of Blood, otherwise you'll be locked out of Tanith's dialogue regarding Rya.

sections.markdown: War Counselor Iji**, also known as **Smithing Master Iji**, is a character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
- War Counselor Iji is an NPC who acts as both a Merchant and a Smithing Table.
- He is found beside the Road to the Manor grace at the northern entrance to Kingsrealm Ruins, located in northwestern Liurnia of the Lakes.
- Iji's questline intersects with the following NPCs: Ranni the Witch, Blaidd the Half-Wolf, Castellan Jerren

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
War Counselor Iji is a wise and kind-hearted Troll who smithed weapons for the Carian royal family and their enchanted knights. He has known Ranni and Blaidd since they were children, and they would let him join in when they played. Along with Blaidd, he swore allegiance to Ranni when she renounced her flesh and chose the dark path of the Empyrean.

He made weapons for Radahn during the Shattering but now counsels and aids Ranni the Witch in her opposition to the Greater Will.

sections.heading: Game events
sections.markdown:
Iji maintains a smithing post near the Kingsrealm Ruins and warns the player to beware Caria Manor. If the played joins Ranni's followers, Iji welcomes them with open arms.

Jerren recalls that the weapons Iji smithed were blunt, yet did not decay when faced with Scarlet Rot. Jerren may also offer a vital clue regarding Ranni's fate, which helps Iji to come to the realisation that General Radahn must be killed in order to release the stars and Ranni's own fate.

Iji is also shown to care for Blaidd, however he also harbours some reservations. Fearing that, as her sworn shadow, Blaidd will go mad and become a curse for Ranni for resisting the Two Fingers, Iji imprisons Blaidd in the Forlorn Hound Evergaol. Later, after Blaidd breaks free of his imprisonment and gives his life in defence of Ranni, Iji admits that he misjudged Blaidd's loyalty, and senses that he will soon join Blaidd in death. Later, he can be found dead, his body ablaze with black flame, with the corpses of Black Knife Assassins nearby.

sections.heading: Questline steps
sections.markdown:
1. Speak to Iji at Road to the Manor, past Kingsrealm Ruins.
 - If Blaidd’s quest is active, choose “Blaidd sent me” to unlock a new shop item.
1. After entering Ranni’s service, speak to his projection at Ranni's Rise.
 - Optional: Ask about Blaidd or Jerren after progressing Ranni’s questline.
1. After Radahn’s defeat, revisit Iji for information about Nokron.
1. After giving Ranni the Dark Moon Ring, defeat Blaidd and return to Iji.
1. Reload the area to find Iji slain. Collect his helm and bell bearing.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Iji does not enter combat and will disappear if attacked. He can be returned by gaining Absolution at the Church of Vows.
- Iji wears an upscaled version of the Nox Mirrorhelm.
- Iji forged glintstone armaments for the Carians and their vassals. Jerren notes Iji's dull weapons resist Scarlet Rot.
 - Iji is possibly one of the armorers who served Radahn, possibly tying him to the Redmanes during the Battle of Aeonia.
- Iji first became acquainted with Jerren when he was a guest of the Carians.
- He is an avid reader.
- After Iji is killed by Black Knife Assassins, his body burns with Blackflame.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Trolls affected by the Power of Corpse Wax and Destined Death (Status Effect) incorrectly burn with blackflame visual effects. This bug explains why War Counselor Iji burns with blackflame after his scripted death.
 - This is untrue as of (at least) Patch 1.16.1. However, the visual effect for Iji is still that of blackflame.

sections.markdown: Vyke the Dragonspear**, also known as **Roundtable Knight Vyke** and **Festering Fingerprint Vyke**, is a character in Elden Ring. He acts as an Invader and a Boss.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Vyke was a Tarnished champion better known for being the closest to becoming Elden Lord before the arrival of the player protagonist.

He was a member of Leyndell's Ancient Dragon Cult, through which he met Lansseax. She shared with him Ancient Dragon incantations and he soon became her most beloved knight. Vyke's mastery grew and he developed his own incantation—Vyke's Dragonbolt, a signature move that electrified his body and lance—earning him the nickname *Vyke the Dragonspear*.

Vyke went on to join the Roundtable Hold, where he was known as the *Roundtable Knight*. "No other Tarnished was closer to the throne of the Elden Lord than Vyke. But, without announcement, Vyke traveled far below the capital, and was scorched by the flame of frenzy." It is believed he either did it for his maiden, or was lured there by other force. According to a Stranded Soul, he was expected to then become the Lord of Frenzied Flame but, for some reason, he didn't. Instead, he was imprisioned in an Evergaol, although he still invades those who approach the Church of Inhibition near the Frenzied Flame Village.

sections.heading: Festering Fingerprint Vyke  (Invader)
sections.markdown:
A dark spirit who invades in Liurnia of the Lakes, on the path leading to the Church of Inhibition.

Vyke will use Vyke's War Spear along with several Frenzy Flame spells. Like other humanoid invaders, he will heal with a Flask of Crimson Tears if needed.

sections.heading: Roundtable Knight Vyke  (Boss)
sections.markdown:
This mini-boss version is found at the Mountaintops of the Giants in the Lord Contender's Evergaol, close to the First Church of Marika (just west of it) on a hill that you can jump up to.

Uses Ancient Dragon Incantations, has a Flask of Crimson Tears, and uses a unique jump attack with his spear. His movements are usually slow and easy to predict, although his abilities can easily kill anyone with low lightning protection. Unlike his Festering Fingerprint form, Vyke does not use any Frenzy abilities during this fight.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Vyke has no dialogue.
- Finger Reader Enia mentions that "Only once before [has she] seen two Great Runes together". This is probably a reference to Vyke, since he is the only one who ever got close to be Elden Lord. Nevertheless, not any other details are given about the situation and Vyke isn't ever mentioned anywhere as having had runes.

- Overall is slightly stronger on Dexterity-scaling affinities.

 - Also uses the Katana dual wield moveset when wielded alongside another Wakizashi, though this will not cause the damage increase for the Wakizashi in the left-hand slot.
- Consistently the strongest dagger damage-wise for all affinities despite its often only average scaling, in large part due to its high base damage. However, it effectively lacks access to the powerful Daggers dual wield moveset and the one for Katanas is much slower and as such will have much worse status build-up.
- The innate Blood Loss build-up pairs well with the extra status build-up from Cold and Occult affinities: the former for the added Frostbite build-up and the latter for the added scaling to the Blood Loss build-up.
- The innate Blood Loss build-up scales with any Arcane-scaling granted by affinities (Poison, Blood, and Occult).
 - While the Blood affinity grants the exact same amount of build-up and scaling as with any other dagger, it does cause the Blood Loss procs to deal an extra 100 flat damage.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Two Fingers** are a set of NPC characters in Elden Ring. Seven pairs of Two Fingers can be found throughout the Lands Between.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown: The Two Fingers are a large, hand-like creature with a slight indentation in its palm and twinned phalange-like appendages, hence their name. When standing upright, these fingers resemble heads with long and wispy white hair. Bowed with age, the Two Fingers are in a state of decay, with exposed flesh and lesions covering their ancient bodies.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The Two Fingers are the children of Metyr, Mother of Fingers, and serve the Lands Between as divine envoys of the Greater Will. They are responsible for selecting Empyreans, granting them shadowbound beasts, and guiding them toward godhood and inheriting the Elden Ring. They are the source of the Baleful Shadows and all Two Fingers incantations and possess the ability to restore blessings to Great Runes atop the ancient Divine Towers. They communicate in a cipher-like language of light composed of intangible symbols that hang in the air, which are perceived and translated by attending Finger Readers. In the past, the Fingers were masters of oration, their wisdom attracting champions from far and wide, establishing missionary churches in foreign realms beyond the Sea of Fog. However, their guidance became skewed long, long ago when their mother was damaged and consequently lost direct contact with the Greater Will.

In a prior age, a pair of Two Fingers deemed Marika an Empyrean and granted her Gurranq, Beast Clergyman. Under their guidance, she wove the Erdtree into existence from a Golden Seed and the primordial Crucible of life. They also selected Ranni, Malenia, Miquella, and the Gloam-Eyed Queen to be gods of the new age. After no clear victor emerged from the Shattering War, the Two Fingers abandoned the Demigods. Their favor was instead granted to the Tarnished, to whom the Grace of Gold had returned, issuing their instructions from the Roundtable Hold. Though most Tarnished follow their teachings, others doubt their judgment and have lost faith. They believe the Two Fingers to be corrupt and senile, having been broken along with the Erdtree long ago. The Two Fingers grant Darkness to confessors who hunt down these enemies.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.markdown:
The first pair of Two Fingers can be found in Roundtable Hold, behind a set of doors that remain closed until the player Tarnished acquires their first Great Rune. They will be at the back of the chamber with Finger Reader Enia sitting close by. Five are found atop Divine Towers; however, each is dormant and lifeless. The seventh chose Ranni the Witch, and is concealed beneath the Cathedral of Manus Celes. She slays it with the Fingerslayer Blade during her questline to fully free herself from its control.

sections.markdown: The **Three Fingers** (三本指, *Sanbonyubi*), also known as the **Readerless Fingers**, are a character in Elden Ring. As the maddening source of Frenzied Flame Incantations, the burnt **Fingers** bestow the Frenzied Flame so that a Lord of Frenzied Flame may rise to destroy the world and return the universe to its primal state before the Greater Will fractured the One Great. They only appear during a cutscene triggered when the player opens the charred door at the bottom of the Frenzied Flame Proscription.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown: As their name implies, the Three Fingers resemble a disembodied humanoid hand with three finger-like appendages, similar to that of the Greater Will's Two Fingers. However, unlike their counterparts, the Three Fingers are burned and smoldering, as they embody the curse of the Frenzied Flame. They emit a frail light that can be felt at the back of the eyes of those who amass Shabriri Grapes. They sear their fingerprints onto the flesh and eyes of those they grasp.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Long ago, the Three Fingers inscribed their message on the great stone tomb of an ancient god. Shabriri, a blind man, was said to have been the first to contact the Fingers and receive the Frenzied Flame. Others would gain audience with the Three Fingers over the ages, though none possessed the strength required melt it all away as a true Lord of Frenzied Flame.

At some point, the Three Fingers were present in Midra's Manse. Among those they embraced was Sage Midra, whom they chose to become the Lord of Frenzied Flame.

During the age of the Erdtree, the Three Fingers were summoned beneath Leyndell, Royal Capital by a curse of despair chanted by the deeply unforgiving Great Caravan. The Fingers enthralled them and their nomadic descendants. After the Shattering, Roundtable Knight Vyke met the Three Fingers, but ultimately failed to rise as a Lord of Chaos.

sections.heading: Location
sections.markdown: Three Fingers reside at the very bottom of the Subterranean Shunning-Grounds, within the Frenzied Flame Proscription. The area is hidden behind an Illusory Wall located at the back of the Cathedral of the Forsaken, and is sealed until Morgott, the Omen King is defeated. Once there, the door can only be opened if the player removes all equipped Armor. The Three Fingers will be in a small chamber behind the door, appearing during a brief cutscene.

sections.heading: Lord of Frenzied Flame
sections.markdown: Interacting with the Three Fingers causes Melina to leave permanently, vowing to kill the player Tarnished. However, the player can now bypass her sacrifice by using the Fingers' flame as kindling to awaken the Flame of Ruin at the Forge of the Giants and commit the Cardinal Sin. The player can still meet the Three Fingers if they have already used Melina to burn the Erdtree. The Three Fingers do not clasp the player again if they cheat fate by inserting Miquella's Needle at the storm beyond time.

sections.markdown: is an unseen character mentioned in Elden Ring. **Rosus Statues** are two sets of interactable objects that emit **Rosus' Light**.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown:
Bowed with age, Rosus is a long-necked, near-skeletal humanoid with a pronounced hunchback and stooped posture. A stoic frown forms on his eyeless face, which is striated like tree bark, and a row of dead twig-like horns grows from his forehead in a regal manner reminiscent of a crown. His hands feature five clawed fingers, but his feet bear only four digits, including a dewclaw. He wears a robe with drooping sleeves and a pin that resembles an eight-spoked wheel.

Statues of Rosus around in the overworld hold a small dish with a black candle in their right hands that, when ignited, produces a trail of blue light not unlike the golden Guidance of Grace. Rosus statues found in Hero's Grave dungeons lack the candle and instead hold a scepter-like torch with both hands that can project a gold Erdtree Burial spell sigil onto the ground by shining light.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: Rosus was the Usher of Death, a psychopomp who guided Those Lost in Death back to the roots for Erdtree Burial. Statues in his likeness appeared across the entire Lands Between, revealing the path to the catacombs with a trail of spectral light. However, it is unclear whether Rosus was a real character or a personification used for religious iconography.

sections.heading: Rosus Candle Statues
sections.markdown: Rosus Statues in the overworld display a message and create an arrow-like trail of blue Rosus Light when activated, ushering the player towards the entrance of a nearby catacombs. If the location is undiscovered, marker icons for the Rosus Statue and its Rosus Light () appear on the Lands Between map.

sections.heading: Rosus Scepter Statues
sections.markdown:
A limited number of Hero's Graves contain "shades"—shadowy enemies that are invulnerable until they are given form by Rosus's gold Light, which projects golden Erdtree Burial sigils onto the ground. Several of the statues must be located and activated before they can shine their light from their scepters.

Statues of Rosus with scepters that emit gold light can be found in the following Hero's Graves:

- Auriza Hero's Grave
- Giant-Conquering Hero's Grave
- Sainted Hero's Grave

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Rosus' Axe is locked behind an Imp Seal in the Black Knife Catacombs. Its unique Skill, Rosus's Summons, is a variant of Tibia's Summons, which also manifests Those Lost in Death.
- Rosus cranes his neck like Deathbirds and Gravebirds.
- Rosus serves a role similar to those of Tibia Mariners and lamplight.
- Rosus Statues with blue light have a similar gameplay function as the spectral Candletrees that lead the player to Caves and other points of interest.
- Disabled Rosus Candle Statues litter the ground near the entrances to Darklight Catacombs, Fog Rift Catacombs, and Scorpion River Catacombs in the Realm of Shadow.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - Rosus is a Latin word, the perfect passive participle of *rōdō* (“gnaw, eat away.”). An appropriate English translation would be *one who has been eaten away*.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **twinbird** was an unseen character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown: The twinbird is an envoy of an Outer God of Death and is the mother of the deathbirds. It is portrayed as a two-headed bird with contrasting features. The feathers of the left head are a vivid, bright red, while the right head's plumage is a deep, rich blue.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
The twinbird once made its nest in the Lands Between, long before the Erdtree grew. The twinbird's offspring were the deathbirds who burned all manner of Death in their ghostflame kilns. Vengeful spirits were released by the ancient death hex as the deathbirds raked the smoldering ashes with barbed bone pokers. Even the putrescent sludge interred within the monolithic stone coffins received these final rites.

The servants of Death venerated the violent Deathbirds as evil deities, symbolically invoking them during sacrificial rituals. Meaningful death was valued, as those who faced death with valor were granted a glorious end. Other worshippers preserved their lives in hopes of making a greater sacrifice in the future.

Over time, the influence of the twinbird waned. Some priests pledged their spears to protect the Deathbirds, entering the rite of Death in exchange for a promised, distant resurrection. Later, Gravebird golems were created in the Deathbirds' likeness to guard the spiritgraves on the Gravesite Plain. Although a few hexes continued to be practiced in the tower of Enir-Ilim, the importance of the ghostflame diminished, and its secrets were eventually forgotten.

When the Prince of Death spread his Deathroot through the roots of the Greattree, the Golden Order collapsed. Soon, the Deathbirds returned to the world as Those Who Live in Death. A few were rumored to descend from above under the cover of night in places where crumbled ruins have fallen from the temple in the sky.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The twinbird is believed to persist in some form or capacity.
- Some speculate that the two-headed bird relief in Crumbling Farum Azula depicts the twinbird.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Wandering Mausoleums** are large, mobile structures in Elden Ring which serve as means to duplicate Remembrances.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
The Wandering Mausoleums are the resting places of soulless demigods who are Marika's unwanted children. They take the form of large buildings mounted atop four legs, which wander around set areas throughout the Lands Between. Some Mausoleums have massive bells hanging from the undersides of their structures which can be heard from afar, ringing to constantly mourn its soulless demigods. Most have skull-like formations in their feet which disappear and release a small amount of ghostflame when hit.

They are often guarded by Mausoleum Knights and Mausoleum Soldiers, who beheaded themselves in order to follow their masters into death, a self-inflicted curse that ties their spirits to the land. Their armor depicts the mausoleum bell, and the knights don wing-shaped ornamentations that evoke the Deathbirds.

The shields of the Mausoleum Knights is emblazoned with the eclipsed sun, which is a symbol of the Mausoleums. The eclipse is the protective star of the soulless demigods and aids the Mausoleum Knights in keeping Destined Death at bay.

sections.heading: Mechanics
sections.markdown:
To use mausoleums and do the process of Remembrance duplication, the player needs to enter a Wandering Mausoleum and interact with the headless corpse on the altar inside. Duplication can only be performed once per mausoleum. Remembrances belonging to Shardbearers may only be duplicated at Wandering Mausoleums with bells, while all other Remembrances can be duplicated at any Wandering Mausoleum (as shown on the table below). Remembrances can be duplicated even after they have already been used.

Typically, access to Wandering Mausoleums is granted by hitting the white skull-shaped forms found on the structure's feet, causing the Mausoleum to lower itself to a height where the player can climb onto them. In most cases, Mausoleum Knights, Mausoleum Soldiers, and Mausoleum Footsoldiers will spawn near the Wandering Mausoleums, serving as an additional obstacle to the player's access to the structures.

sections.heading: Weeping Peninsula
sections.markdown: A Wandering Mausoleum can be found on the western side of Weeping Peninsula, south-east of the Fourth Church of Marika. To gain entry, attack the skull-like deposits on its legs until they disappear, while avoiding its footfalls. Once enough have been destroyed, the Wandering Mausoleum will lower itself to the ground.

sections.markdown: Found to the north-east of the Academy of Raya Lucaria, guarded by several groups of Mausoleum Soldiers and Knights. Since the skull deposits are located on the rocky plateau around the Mausoleum itself, the player must make use of a spirit spring to get on top of the Mausoleum in order to destroy them.

sections.heading: Liurnia of the Lakes (Uld Palace Ruins)
sections.markdown: Two Wandering Mausoleums can be found in the Uld Palace Ruins region in the east of Liurnia of the Lakes. Unlike every other Wandering Mausoleum, these two lack bells, and no Mausoleum Knights or Soldiers are found nearby. These are also the only Wandering Mausoleums where Remembrances which come from Shardbearer bosses cannot be duplicated. In addition to stomping, these Mausoleums can jump up in the air, creating a shockwave when they land which can damage the player.

sections.heading: Deeproot Depths
sections.markdown: A single Wandering Mausoleum can be found in the north-western section of Deeproot Depths, guarded by many Mausoleum Knights and Soldiers. The skull-like growths are all on the upper part of the structure, so the player must jump onto it from the large roots found nearby.

sections.markdown: A Wandering Mausoleum can be found outside Castle Sol in the Mountaintops of the Giants. This Mausoleum is not guarded by Mausoleum Knights or Soldiers and the growths are all found on its legs, making it relatively easy to gain access to.

sections.markdown: Thrusting Swords** are a type of melee armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
They possess on average low weight, low stamina cost on attacking, quick attack speed and reasonable range at the cost of low damage against health, poise and the stamina of guarding opponents. Their subtle telegraphs at the start of most of their attack animations make it difficult for other players to react to, which turns them into excellent sidearms when dual-wielded alongside most other weapon types. Similar to Curved Swords their heavy attack charges can be canceled in favor of a quick feint-attack should the player press the Roll button while charging. They can also attack while guarding at the same time similar to Heavy Thrusting Swords and Spears.

Their two-handed moveset is generally very similar to their one-handed one, increasing overall damage to poise and health at the cost of the perks gained from being used alongside other weapons and shields.

Their dual-wielded moveset consists of flurries of several smaller, lower-damage attacks of varying numbers per button press, allowing one to inflict status ailments faster at the cost of committing to longer-lasting attack animations and delayed recovery from said attacks.

sections.markdown: Vargram the Raging Wolf** is an NPC in *Elden Ring*.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.markdown:
Vargram was one of the first Tarnished to visit Roundtable Hold. He earned his nickname from the white wolf pelt that adorns his helm. Vargram aspired to attain the status of a wolf, based on the old legend that wolves are shadows of the Empyreans.

Vargram was a friend of Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm, however guidance led the two into confrontation with one another, and Wilhelm was taken prisoner in Roundtable Hold.

The Tarnished encounters Vargram and Wilhelm together in the Fortified Manor in Leyndell, Royal Capital, during a joint mission with Knight Bernahl on behalf of the Volcano Manor.

Version 1.00 was markedly different from the final build of *Elden Ring*. It is only accessible by installing and playing the disc version of the game without an internet connection.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **Vulgar Militia**, **Black Blade Vulgar Militia**, and **Shadow Militia** are Enemies in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown: In the Lands Between, people of small stature were despised and disgraced, and many banded together as the vulgar militia to survive, earning their squalid keep in dishonor. Estranged and hostile toward outsiders, they became the tireless wardens of desolate fringes, unsung battlefields, and places deliberately stricken from memory. The militia lurked among the countless stinking corpses left by both the War Against the Giants and the crusade across the Realm of Shadow. Rumors circulated that they sustained their numbers by hacking apart the dead.

sections.heading: Characteristics
sections.markdown:
The tiny Vulgar Militiamen are witty, acrobatic combatants who ambush and overwhelm their much-larger opponents with weapons particularly effective at causing Blood Loss, including chain-sickles, hooked sickles, and long-hafted, serrated saws. Some Vulgar Militiamen toss smoke bombs, while others place small, spikey traps coated in a green liquid that, when triggered, release lingering gas clouds that inflict Poison buildup. They are fully immune to Poison.

Black Black Vulgar Militia cast Bestial Incantations like Beast Claw. They can imbue their weapons with an affinity similar to Black Blade and the Power of Corpse Wax.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: The **War against the Giants**, refers to the conflict in the Lands Between between the forces of Leyndell and the Fire Giants.

sections.heading: Background
sections.markdown:
Long ago, the red-haired Fire Giants had made the northern Mountaintops their lands, after chasing away the ice dragons who were the former lords of the region. The Giants worshiped the God of Fire, whose one-eyed visage manifested upon their chests, and continued to borrow its power and practice smithing as a form of divine ritual, and even the Trolls, their descendants, wielded hammers as ceremonial tools for smithing, crafted with the same pattern of the fell god's eye.

Meanwhile, Queen Marika the Eternal, the Empyrean that become the vessel of the Elden Ring, had planted the Golden Seed that would become the Erdtree under the guidance of the Two Fingers and had begun to establish her reign over the Lands Between. The Flame of Ruin posed a threat to the burgeoning Erdtree, as it was capable of burning it, and thus needed to be neutralized for her Order to truly start. And so, Queen Marika and her consort Godfrey, First Elden Lord, marched upon the Mountaintops of the Giants.

sections.heading: Battles
sections.markdown:
The War against the Giants, was led by Godfrey himself. When the king of the battlefield and his warriors left the Altus plateau and reached into the Mountaintops they joined forces with the Knights of Zamor, who had been historical and mortal enemies of the Fire Giants, having challenged them many times in the past thanks to the power of their ice storms.

From the town of Zamor the allied forces marched through the Mountaintops, carving winding paths to reach the higher, western summit on the other side of the cliff walls.. The fighting continued, with the Giants using their bellowing roars to trigger avalanches and whip up storms of flame, and facing a Fire Giant was seen as a horror, thanks to their dreadful visages and the power of the flames they wielded.

Enormous, crushing weapons were deployed to counter their onslaught, and the heroes of the Erdtree strengthened their arms using semi-vitrified smithing stones mined in the cold, northern regions. The priest of the Erdtree would devise a fire incantation to protect the warriors of Godfrey from the Giants' flame. However this defense was created through that same fire, thus requiring for priests of the Erdtree to have faith in the Fell God they were fighting

After traversing the great lake of the Mountaintops, now closer the the Forge of the Giants, Queen Marika issued a proclamation to Godfrey and his warriors, commanding them to put the Giants to the sword and confine their flame, so that the Age of the Erdtree could begin.

At some point, the Trolls, the descendants of the Giants, betrayed their ancestors and switched sides to fight on behalf of the Erdtree and were furnished with gilded swords to commemorate their fealty.

Despite the initial odds, the champions of the Erdtree prevailed over the Fire Giants that were massacred in the fields before their Forge, leaving the battlefield littered with their impaled corpses. Queen Marika herself supposedly fought against the one-eyed fell god, and she was believed to have been slain them.

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.markdown:
Although the Giants had been defeated, it became apparent that the Flame of Ruin would never die and the fell god was still lurking within the last Fire Giant.. Seeing this, Queen Marika marked the lone surviving Fire Giant with a curse, compelling him to tend to the flame for eternity.

With the flame sealed away, the Fire Monks and Flame Guardians were appointed to watch over its smoldering remains.. Wearing armor emblazoning with a depictions of the fell god of the Giants to imprint the idea of taboo through fear these priest warriors also continued to make use of Giants' Flame Incantations that required faith in it through Giant's Seal depicting the god of the Giants. The Fire Prelates kept the Fire Giant incantations hidden and the Chief Guardian Arghanthy kept the legendary Flame of the Fell God incantation drawing directly from power of the fell god a secret After many years of watch, the Fire Monks would later succumb to the allure of the flame,

The Giant-Conquering Hero's Grave was built to give Erdtree Burial to the champions that fought in the war, even becoming the resting place of dozens of Trolls that fought alongside the Erdtree's warriors.

The knights of Zamor earned great renown for their actions during the war and were hailed as heroes. Some of them would leave from their ancestral home to continue to fight under the Erdtree, their devotion showing even centuries later as some of them would defend the Hero's Graves of the War against the Giants and the Ancient Dragons The Trolls, despite their own efforts in the war, did not receive such recognition and were instead merely integrated into the army as war beasts and would end up used as menial labor, working in mines, or dragging great coffin carriages when their intelligence degraded.

The end of the war marked the dawn of the Erdtree's era, presided over by Queen Marika and Godfrey. The Erdtree itself would go on to become the embodiment of Order and its blessed sap dripping from its boughs would start an Age of Plenty.

Although the flame of ruin was sealed, the burning of the Erdtree was considered to be the first cardinal sin. Prophets would occasionally glimpse the flame of ruin in their faith, envisioning the ruin that it would bring. Those who had such visions would be banished, forced to wear shackles around their necks to warn passersby against listening to them.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Unique Skill: Glintstone Dart** is a Skill in Elden Ring. It is exclusive to the Glintstone Kris.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Fires a Magic projectile with 155 base Magic Attack Power and resembles Great Glintstone Shard when uncharged and Glintstone Cometshard when charged, with the base Attack Power also increasing to 190 when charged.
Using a heavy attack afterwards initiates a long-range thrust, hitting with 170% of the weapon's Attack Power.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Essentially a version of the Skill: Glintstone Pebble that costs 2 more FP and where the projectile is chargeable, granting a 23% Attack Power increase.
- The projectile scales purely of off Intelligence while the thrust depends on the weapon's own Attack Power, meaning it benefits mainly from Dexterity and Intelligence.
 - Will always have at least 620 (760 if charged) Attack Power at +10.
 - At +10 and with minimum weapon requirement stats, 20 Intelligence, it has 665 Attack Power (815 Attack Power if charged), at 45 Intelligence it has 702 Attack Power (860 Attack Power if charged), at 60 Intelligence the beam has 715 Attack Power (876 Attack Power if charged), and at 80 Intelligence it has 726 Attack Power (890 Attack Power if charged).
 - At 80 Intelligence the regular version of the skill is equivalent in Attack Power to a regular Comet spell cast with 249 Sorcery Scaling while the charged version is equivalent in Attack Power to a charged Comet spell cast with 244 Sorcery Scaling.
- The projectile benefits from the Godfrey Icon when charged, increasing the Attack Power by a further 15% (41% total Attack Power increase).
- As a Magic-based skill it benefits from the Spellblade's Set Attack Power bonus.
- While the projectile deals no Stance damage, the follow-up thrust deals a whopping 30, more than any other dagger attack (the strongest dagger attack normally is the charged heavy attack, with 18 Stance damage).
 - This is considerably more Stance damage than the Glintstone Pebble skill, which on a dagger will deal 3 Stance damage on the projectile and 12 on the follow-up thrust.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.06 increased the range of the projectile but decreased the damage and the stagger, preventing the projectile and the thrust from chaining into each other automatically.
- Patch 1.07 increased the range, speed and damage of the magic projectile and made it penetrate through enemies when uncharged.
 - The base Attack Power of the uncharged and charged projectiles were increased from 140 to 155 and from 170 to 190 respectively.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown: Prevents the loss of Runes upon death for 3 minutes (except for deaths caused by Death Blight).

This is of course presuming you are carrying a worthwhile amount of runes.
- Keep in mind the time limit, as while 3 minutes is a fair amount of time it's still a limited amount of time and it may run out at the worst of times in an area.
 - Usually best saved for a run through or fight against dangerous enemies, or just before starting a section with falls.
- Can be used to transport out a bunch of Runes stuck inside of a boss room, especially when combined with quitting out to the main menu to reset the character to just outside of the boss room's fog wall.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Unique Skill: Blade of Gold** is a Skill in Elden Ring. It is exclusive to the Blade of Calling.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown: User leaps into the air and then throws out a projectile with 145 base Holy Attack Power that also launches foes backward.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Attack Power scales with weapon upgrade level and user Faith.
 - Will always have at least 580 Attack Power at +10.
 - At +10 and with minimum weapon requirement stats, 15 Faith, it has 756 Attack Power, at 45 Faith it has 1010 Attack Power, at 60 Faith the beam has 1079 Attack Power, and at 80 Faith it has 1138 Attack Power.
- Grants heavy hyperarmor when mid-air, effectively making the skill almost impossible to interrupt after leaping up.
- Generally outclassed by the Black Knife's Blade of Death skill. While this one is fairly strong against weaker enemies (and even some of the heavier ones such as Omens) due to the high damage and ability to throw them away, it doesn't do as well against Bosses due to them steadily gaining more and more Holy damage negation from the point where this skill's weapon is acquired and the Blade of Death's percentage-based damage will gold up better against the ever increasing HP totals of later bosses.
 - The reason this skill deals more damage before the percentage-based damage even though Blade of Death has higher base damage is because the Blade of Calling's higher base Faith scaling results in a stronger multiplier for the damage.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - The cost of the skill was reduced from 20 FP to 17 FP at an unknown point as an unlisted change.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Unique Skill: Blade of Death** is a Skill in Elden Ring. It is exclusive to the Black Knife.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
User leaps into the air and then throws out a projectile with 180 base Holy Attack Power that briefly staggers foes.

Reduces maximum HP of hit enemies by 10% for 15 seconds and drains their HP by roughly 4% over the course of 5 seconds.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Attack Power scales with weapon upgrade level and user Faith.
 - Will always have at least 720 Attack Power at +10.
 - At +10 and with minimum weapon requirement stats, 20 Faith, it has 856 Attack Power, at 45 Faith it has 969 Attack Power, at 60 Faith the beam has 1009 Attack Power, and at 80 Faith it has 1043 Attack Power.
- Grants heavy hyperarmor when mid-air, effectively making the skill almost impossible to interrupt after leaping up.
- The max HP reduction effect stacks with either the Black Blade Incantation or Destined Death skill's similar max HP reduction, as those two use a similar but slightly different effect to the Blade of Death's effect.
- Since a large part of the damage is percentage-based the Faith-scaling is less important than it otherwise would be.
 - For comparison: a +10 Black Knife wielded with 80 Faith has 7.6% more Attack Power with Blade of Death than one used with 45 Faith (like a hybrid 45/45 Dexterity/Faith build) and 22% more Attack Power than a Blade of Death used with 20 Faith (barely above minimum requirements).
- The comparatively stronger base Attack Power of the projectile doesn't quite compensate for the Black Knife's comparatively lower base Faith-scaling.

sections.heading: See also
sections.markdown:

- Unique Skill: Destined Death, the other unique skill that deals percentage-based damage

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Unique Skill: Golden Tempering** is a Skill in Elden Ring. It is exclusive to the Ornamental Straight Sword.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
- Crosses the blades, granting a 100 Holy damage buff.
 - Using a heavy attack when buffed in this way uses both weapons to perform a quick dual thrust, each dealing damage equal to 105% of weapon Attack Power.
 - Using a partially charged heavy attack when buffed in this way unleashes 3 quick thrusts for damage equal to 45% of weapon Attack Power per thrust, before ending with the same dual thrust as the uncharged version, each dealing damage equal to 105% of weapon Attack Power.
 - Using a fully charged heavy attack when buffed in this way unleashes a flurry of 10 quick thrusts for damage equal to 45% of weapon Attack Power per thrust, before ending with the same dual thrust as the uncharged version, each dealing damage equal to 125% of weapon Attack Power.
 - Using a running heavy attack when buffed in this way uses both weapons to perform a quick, dashing dual thrust.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Each quick thrust costs 2 points of Stamina while the final thrusts cost 9 points of Stamina each.
 - The uncharged heavy costs 2*9=18 points of Stamina.
 - The uncharged heavy costs 3*2+2*9=24 points of Stamina.
 - The uncharged heavy costs 10*2+2*9=38 points of Stamina.
- Deals a pitiful 20 Stance damage with the charged heavy attack, 1 point per attack in the flurry and then 10 for the final dual thrust. The uncharged version deals 10 Stance damage.
- If the buff ends when a special attack is being performed, the attack will continue being performed, it just can't be used again unless the skill is reused to reapply the buff.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.07 added a timing for interrupting the attack during a series of strong attacks while under the effect, increased strong attack motion speed, poise damage, and stamina attack power against guarding enemies during the effect, increased the duration and attack power of the effect that grants the weapon a holy attribute, reduced time between the skill activation and being able to perform actions.
 - Increased the duration of the skill's weapon buff from 40 seconds to 60 seconds, and increased the amount of added Holy damage from 85 to 100. It also decreased the aftercast time where you are unable to do anything after performing the skill.
- Patch 1.04 decreased FP cost and increased cast speed, and increased effect duration.
 - FP cost was reduced from 30 to 24, and the duration was increased from 20 seconds to 40 seconds.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Unique Skill: Last Rites** is a Skill in Elden Ring. It is exclusive to the Golden Epitaph.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown: Increases weapon damage for user and all nearby allies by 10% (5% in PvP) plus a flat 25 extra Holy damage (both only for weapon attacks) and grants 100% bonus damage against Those Who Live in Death for all attacks, all for 60 seconds. This counts as an Aura Buff.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- As this is an Aura Buff it is directly in competition with the spell Golden Vow, a contest it falls short of on a build with enough Faith and FP to cast the latter. However, since the weapon this is attached to still scales fairly well with only one of or both of Strength and Dexterity it still has a niche. Even more so, it is always holds the niche of being generally significantly stronger than either Golden Vow again against Those Who Live in Death.
 - Note that Last Rites almost only increases weapon damage, meaning Golden Vow is always better for spells.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.12 fixed a bug that caused damage to the player and friendly summons when using the "Last Rites" Skill under specific circumstances.
 - Prior to the fix, Last Rites would be applied to non-damaging effects such as Terra Magica or Great Heal, making them deal the flat 25 Holy damage to any friendly players standing on it.
- Patch 1.07 increased effect duration, increased attack power, effect against Those Who Live in Death has been revised upward.
 - The skill's duration was increased from 45 seconds to 60 seconds, the universal 10% damage buff was added (limited to 5% in PvP), and the damage bonus against Those Who Live in Death was increased from 50% to 100%.
- Patch 1.04 increased cast speed.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Unique Skill: Eochaid's Dancing Blade** is a Skill in Elden Ring. It is exclusive to the Regalia of Eochaid and Marais Executioner's Sword.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Throws the sword forwards telekinetically and spins it, hitting 7 times to hit for 35% of weapon Attack Power each (245% of weapon Attack Power total). After the sword returns to the wielder's hand to hit for 82% of weapon Attack Power, it's used to slash once diagonally, for damage equal to 95% of weapon Attack Power (damage equal to 422% of weapon Attack Power for the entire skill).

Can be charged to hold the spin for longer and thus deliver more and stronger hits. Increases amount of hits on the spins to 10 and damage per spin to 40% of weapon Attack Power (400% of weapon Attack Power total), damage of the returning hit to 100% of weapon Attack Power, and damage on the finishing slash to 100% of weapon Attack Power (damage equal to 600% of weapon Attack Power for the entire charged skill).

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- The skill costs 20 points of Stamina to use, 10 for starting the spins and 10 for doing the follow-up swing. Charging the skill increases Stamina cost to 24 points, as the start and end both increase to 12 points of Stamina each.
- Deals more damage on the Marais Executioner's Sword since both weapons have the same multipliers on the skill and it has higher Attack Power.
- Since damage depends on the used weapon's Attack Power and both weapons that have this skill partially deal Magic damage (about a third of their total Attack Power), this skill actually benefits fairly well from things that increase that element such as Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear and Terra Magica.
- Damage is boosted by the Godfrey Icon if charged.
- One of a few skills that actually works with repeated-hits boosters such as the Winged Sword Insignias and Thorny Cracked Tear.
- It's possible to roll, and thus cancel the skill, after the spin has been performed, meaning it's not necessary to perform the slash at the end. This will however reduce damage for the uncharged and charged versions of the skill by 23% and 17% respectively.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Patch 1.07 reduced the delay between the end of various actions (such as using items or attack animations) and being able to perform the skill.
- Patch 1.04 increased travel distance, added a window to roll during the attack to cancel the animation.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Unique Skill: Unblockable Blade** is a Skill in Elden Ring. It comes in two different variants carrying the same name, each exclusive to the Coded Sword and Cipher Pata respectively.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Takes a step forwards before performing a wide horisontal slash, dealing damage equal to 250% of weapon Attack Power.

Ignores all damage negation from a guarding shield or weapon.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:

- Like the weapon, this skill deals pure Holy damage.
- Deals a heavy 36 Stance damage, more than even a Straight Sword's charged heavy attack. This means that the skill breaks most regular enemies' Stance in 2 hits, and most bosses within 3 or 4 hits if attacking quickly enough.
- Good at managing small crowds of enemies due to its surprisingly great reach and wide hitbox.

sections.heading: Trivia

- Patch 1.04 increased cast speed with the weapon Coded Sword.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Unique Skill: Night-and-Flame Stance** is a Skill in Elden Ring. It is exclusive to the Sword of Night and Flame.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
Holding the skill button puts the user in a stance that slows their movement speed, with two followups:
- light attacks perform a forward thrust that unleashes a miniature Comet Azur, hitting first for 108% of the weapon's Magic Attack Power, then 6 times for 162% of Magic Attack Power, and then one final hit for 194% of Magic Attack Power (1,274% of weapon Magic Attack Power in total).
- heavy attacks makes a sweep that forms a wave of flames, hitting for 800% of the weapon's Fire Attack Power.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Both versions of the skill costs 46 points of Stamina to use.
- The light attack followup causes Magic damage and scales with upgrade level and Intelligence. It is most useful for heavy single-target damage.
- The heavy attack followup causes Fire damage and scales with upgrade level and Faith. It is fairly hard to dodge due to how wide it is and handles crowds of enemies well.
- Carian Filigreed Crest is of high value for this skill due to the high FP costs.
- The Comet Azur-like effect of the light attack followup cannot be channeled, unlike the spell.
- Stance damage is about on par with a charged heavy attack, though the flame wave deals slightly less and the magic beam deals slightly more.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown:
- Despite the description stating that the light attack follow-up casts Night Comet it actually casts Comet Azur.
- Patch 1.07 increased attack power, the attack direction may now be adjusted up and down when using a normal attack, added damage detection to the weapon part.
 - Increased the damage of the light attack follow-up from 100%, 150%, and 180% of weapon Magic Attack Power (1,180% in total) to 108%, 162%, and 194% of Magic Attack Power (1,274% in total).
 - Increased the damage of the heavy attack follow-up from 700% of weapon Fire Attack Power to 800% of Fire Attack Power.
- Patch 1.03 decreased weapon skill, Sword of Night and Flame’s damage.

sections.markdown: Unique Skill: Shriek of Milos** is a Skill in Elden Ring. It is exclusive to the Sword of Milos.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:

- The first heavy attack of Sword of Milos now becomes a three hit combo, and the second heavy attack becomes a slam to the ground with the blade. It is equivalent to the greatsword Barbaric Roar moveset.

sections.markdown: Unique Skill: Alabaster Lords' Pull** is a Skill in Elden Ring. It is exclusive to the Alabaster Lord's Sword.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown: Stabs weapon into the ground before pulling surrounding enemies in with a gravitational wave.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Like Ash of War: Gravitas the pull wave actually consist of 3 overlapping waves, dealing more damage the closer they are to the wielder.
- Both the stab and the waves deal damage.
- Actually mostly deals Physical damage, with a 4-to-1 Physical-to-Magic damage-ratio.
- The Magic portion's damage is boosted by the Spellblade's Set.
- Deals a decent amount of Stance damage, on par with a jumping heavy attack.
- As the description states, has a slightly greater range than Ash of War: Gravitas.
- Brings down flying enemies, as stated in Note: Gravity's Advantage.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.markdown: Ghostflame Ignition** is a Unique Skill in Elden Ring. It is exclusive to the Death's Poker.

sections.heading: Availability
sections.markdown: - Unique Skill: Ghostflame Ignition is only available on the Death's Poker.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.markdown:
- Thrust forwards with the Poker to create a small ball of ghostflame ( 55 base Magic Attack Power) that hits 4 times, then detonates for 140 base if no follow-up is used.
 - Light attack follow-up: sweep through the ball (110% weapon Attack Power) to create a long ghostflame trail, dealing 150 base on spread and 60 base on lingering trail.
 - Heavy attack follow-up: slam the ball to detonate it with 200 base.
- Each hit inflicts 55 Frostbite build-up.
- The initial thrust has high Hyper Armor.

sections.heading: Frame data
sections.markdown:
- Initial thrust on frame 27/0.90s → ball appears frame 29/0.97s → lasts ~2s → explosion frame 43/1.43s
- Light follow-up: sweep frame 71/2.37s → trail spread frame 73/2.43s → ends frame 98/3.27s
- Heavy follow-up: slam frame 67/2.23s → detonation frame 69/2.30s → ends frame 98/3.27s
- Hyper Armor active frame 11/0.37s to frame 37/1.23s

sections.heading: Notes
sections.markdown:
- Costs: 15 FP (follow-ups 10), 14 Stamina (follow-ups 9).
- Explosion Magic Attack Power scales with Intelligence and upgrade level (modified by Death's Poker’s scaling).
 - Minimum Attack Power at max upgrade (+10):
 - 1 INT → ticks 220 / explosion 560 / spread 600 / lingering 240 / detonation 800
 - 11 INT → ticks 236 / explosion 601 / spread 644 / lingering 258 / detonation 858
 - 30 INT → ticks 262 / explosion 667 / spread 715 / lingering 286 / detonation 953
 - 80 INT → ticks 296 / explosion 752 / spread 806 / lingering 323 / detonation 1,074
- Stance damage:
 - Initial thrust 100%
 - Ghostflame ball 1.5 per tick + 4 on explosion
 - Light follow-up: sweep 100%, spread 5 (trail 0)
 - Heavy follow-up: slam 100%, detonation 11
 - Greatsword weapon attacks = 5.5 Stance damage each
 - Thrust (before ball) and slam (before detonation) deal no damage but still inflict small Stance damage
- Only the physical attack tied to each Ghostflame action is parryable.

sections.heading: Strategies
sections.markdown:
- Poor INT scaling makes Terra Magica or Magic-Shrouding Cracked Tear better damage boosts.
- Each piece of Spellblade's Set increases Magic damage by 2%.

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.markdown: - Update 1.06 patched a bug that caused stuttering when hitting large enemies.
